claim: The proportions of astrocytes (Astro), tanycytes (Tany), fibroblasts (Fibro), pars tuberalis cells (PTC), and endothelial cells (Endo) were decreased in aged hypothalamus compared to young.

claim: Significant ligand-receptor pairs Bmp2–Acvr1/Acvr2a/Acvr2b/Bmpr, Gdf11–Acvr2a/Acvr2b, Inhba–Acvr1/Acvr2a/Acvr2b were exclusively and significantly increased in neurons of the aged group.
source: Notably, among the significant ligand–receptor pairs in neurons, Bmp2–Acvr1/Acvr2a/Acvr2b/Bmpr, Gdf11–Acvr2a/Acvr2b, Inhba–Acvr1/Acvr2a/Acvr2b, Nrg1/Nrg2/Nrg4–Erbb4, Rspo1–Lgr5/Lrp6, and Rspo3–Lgr5 were exclusively and significantly increased in neurons of the O group compared to those in O.T and Y, suggesting enhanced TGF superfamily-mediated signaling activity and canonical Wnt signaling during aging.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E showing ligand-receptor interactions.

claim: Enhanced TGF superfamily-mediated signaling activity and canonical Wnt signaling occur during aging in hypothalamic neurons.
source: Notably, among the significant ligand–receptor pairs in neurons, Bmp2–Acvr1/Acvr2a/Acvr2b/Bmpr, Gdf11–Acvr2a/Acvr2b, Inhba–Acvr1/Acvr2a/Acvr2b, Nrg1/Nrg2/Nrg4–Erbb4, Rspo1–Lgr5/Lrp6, and Rspo3–Lgr5 were exclusively and significantly increased in neurons of the O group compared to those in O.T and Y, suggesting enhanced TGF superfamily-mediated signaling activity and canonical Wnt signaling during aging.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed ligand-receptor pair changes.

claim: Ligand-receptor pairs Nlgn1–Nrxn1/Nrxn2, Nlgn2–Nrxn1/Nrxn2/Nrxn3, Nlgn3–Nrxn1/Nrxn2/Nrxn3 were exclusively increased in neurons of 17α-estradiol-treated aged rats.
source: The significantly changed ligand–receptor pairs Nlgn1–Nrxn1/Nrxn2, Nlgn2–Nrxn1/Nrxn2/Nrxn3, Nlgn3–Nrxn1/Nrxn2/Nrxn3, Nxph1–Nrxn1/Nrxn2/Nrxn3, Nxph3–Nrxn1/Nrxn2/Nrxn3, Pomc–Oprd1/Oprk1/Oprm1, and Vip–Adcyap1r1/Avpr1a/Vipr2 were exclusively increased in neurons of O.T compared to O and Y (Figure 1E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1E.

claim: These ligand-receptor pairs were associated with synaptic activity, cellular adhesion, the opioid system, and vasodilation, indicating unique roles of 17α-estradiol in restoring certain physiological functions in the aging hypothalamus.
source: These ligand–receptor pairs were associated with synaptic activity, cellular adhesion, the opioid system, and vasodilation, indicating unique roles of 17α-estradiol in restoring certain physiological functions in the aging hypothalamus.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the observed ligand-receptor changes.

claim: The increased Pomc signal in O.T neurons aligns with previous reports that 17α-estradiol treatment decreases food intake in mice.
source: The increased Pomc signal in O.T neurons aligns with previous reports that 17α-estradiol treatment decreases food intake in mice; this is likely because Pomc neurons promote satiety, and elevated Pomc signaling in O.T may enhance satiety-driven reduction in food uptake (Figure 1E; Steyn et al., 2018).
evidence: This connects the current findings with prior research through citation.

claim: Most top-ranked pathways related to synapses were downregulated in aged neurons, while 17α-estradiol treatment reversed this trend.
source: ROC analysis of significantly differently expressed pathways related to neural synapses, manually selected from Gene Ontology databases, indicated that most top-ranked pathways related to synapses, according to AUC values, were downregulated in aged neurons, while 17α-estradiol treatment reversed this trend (Figure 1G, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1G showing pathway rankings.

claim: Energy metabolism and synapse activity represent two opposing regulatory signaling networks in hypothalamic neurons.
source: Our findings revealed that energy metabolism and synapse activity represent two opposing regulatory signaling networks in hypothalamic neurons, with 17α-estradiol strongly playing a significant role in balancing these networks (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: 17α-estradiol plays a significant role in balancing the two opposing regulatory signaling networks of energy metabolism and synapse activity.
source: Our findings revealed that energy metabolism and synapse activity represent two opposing regulatory signaling networks in hypothalamic neurons, with 17α-estradiol strongly playing a significant role in balancing these networks (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: Transcription factors Calr, Clu, Peg3, Prnp, Ndufa13, Actb, Ywhab, Nfe2l1, Mtdh, Npm1, Bex2, Aft4, and Maged1 were positively correlated with pathways involved in OXPHOS subunits, lysosome function, protein export, mTorc1 signaling, and UPR.
source: For example, Calr, Clu, Peg3, Prnp, Ndufa13, Actb, Ywhab, Nfe2l1, Mtdh, Npm1, Bex2, Aft4, and Maged1 were positively correlated with pathways involved in OXPHOS subunits, lysosome function, protein export, mTorc1 signaling, and the unfolded protein response (UPR) in O, O.T, and Y neurons, while showing negative correlations with pathways related to ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, endocytosis, tight junctions, focal adhesion, axon guidance, and MAPK signaling.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B showing correlation patterns.

claim: TFs Myt1l, Ctnnd2, Tenm4, Camta1, Med12l, Rere, Csrnp3, Erbb4, Jazf1, Dscam, Klf12, and Kdm4c exhibited opposite correlation patterns with selected pathways compared to the first group of TFs.

evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: These TFs may take conserved roles in regulating the two opposing biological processes in hypothalamic neurons.
source: These TFs may take conserved roles in regulating the two opposing biological processes in hypothalamic neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the TF correlation patterns.

claim: The proportion of neurons in aged group decreased from c1 to c4 in metabolic pathways, while this trend was reversed in the opposing signaling pathways.
source: From the distribution patterns, we observed that the proportion of neurons in O decreased from c1 to c4 in metabolic pathways (MitoCarta OXPHOS subunits and Hallmark mTorc1 signaling), while this trend was reversed in the opposing signaling pathways (GOBP synapse organization and KEGG MAPK signaling pathway) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: In young rats, the trend in neuron proportions across quarters was opposite to that in aged rats.
source: In contrast, in Y, this trend was opposite, suggesting the expression levels from the four quarters (c1-c4) of the two opposing signaling networks can be used to monitor aging status.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: Treatment with 17α-estradiol alleviated or reversed the aging-related trend in neuron proportions across quarters.
source: Treatment with 17α-estradiol alleviated this trend or even reversed it in O.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: A c1-up-signature of 19 genes and a c4-up-signature of 12 genes were identified to represent the two opposing signaling networks.
source: Unique markers in c1 (19 genes, c1-up-signature) and c4 (12 genes, c4-up-signature) were identified; however, c2 and c3 lacked unique markers shared by the six pathways (Figure 2D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2D.

claim: The 19 genes in c1-up-signature displayed an inverse correlation pattern with the 12 genes in c4-up-signature.
source: Consequently, the 19 genes in c1-up-signature displayed an inverse correlation pattern with the 12 genes in c4-up-signature, indicating the two opposing gene signatures are capable of reflecting the two opposing signaling networks in hypothalamic neurons (Figure 2E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2E.

claim: The balance of the two opposing signaling networks affected by 17α-estradiol in non-neural cell types was less pronounced than in neurons.
source: Conversely, the balance of the two opposing signaling networks affected by 17α-estradiol in non-neural cell types was less pronounced than in neurons, showing variable effects on non-neural cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Microglia exhibited lower levels of synapse-related cellular processes in O.T compared to O, which was distinct from the observations in neurons.
